summary: Kootenai National Forest crow's nest in Lincoln County, dated 1921. Its lookout, Anton Obermayer, died in an August 1931 fire. Current condition unknown.

facts.design: Crow's nest with an 8-by-8-foot log cabin
facts.status_note: Listed as abandoned by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; the lookout website says the log cabin was still there, but that remark is undated

events.note: Crow's nest with an 8x8 ft log cabin, per the firelookout.com entry for 1921
Lookout Anton (Antone) Obermayer killed by a falling tree while leaving the station; sources name the fire the Keno Mountain fire or the Deer Creek Fire and differ on the night

corrections.why: The FFLA list gives this site's status as Abandoned, which the pipeline mapped to gone (data/sources/ffla.json status_raw). No source records its removal, and firelookout.com says the log cabin was still there, undated. Abandoned is not in the status vocabulary, so unknown is the closest honest value.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's gone value comes from the FFLA word Abandoned. The standing value from firelookout.com rests on an undated remark that the cabin was still there. Neither source describes the site today, so the status is unknown.

sources.title: Deer Creek Fire Lookout Hit by Tree Fatality 1931

notes_for_editor: Name: firelookout.com has Antone Obermayer, the federal page Anton Obermayer, and the quoted 1931 newspaper Anton Obermeyer. Fire: firelookout.com says the Keno Mountain fire; the federal page says the Deer Creek Fire and gives the fuller account. Night: the federal page says the night of August 27; the report, dated August 27, says last night. The 1940s abandonment is undated, so no abandoned event was written. The record's kind platform matches the vocabulary entry for crow's nests. The status mapping of FFLA Abandoned to gone may affect other Montana entries with that word. Current condition is not documented.
